questions.scenario: Your younger sibling is crying because they scraped their knee badly.

options.text: I quickly grab the first-aid kit, clean the blood, and bandage it up fast.
I check if they hit their head or if the cut is deep enough to need a doctor.
I distract them with a funny face or a story while gently cleaning the wound.
I scold them slightly for being careless while making sure they are okay.

questions.scenario: You are assigned duty in the school's 'Medical Room' (Sick Room) for the day.

options.text: I love it when there's a rush of students coming in after getting hurt in the PT period.
I accurately check everyone's temperature and blood pressure using the instruments.
I comfort the students who are just homesick and pretending to have a stomach ache.
I neatly organize the medicine cabinets and update the school medical register.

questions.scenario: Your grandparents have to take 10 different pills a day. How do you help?

options.text: I physically help them sit up, give them water, and make sure they swallow it.
I read the prescriptions carefully and sort the pills exactly by Morning, Noon, and Night.
I sit with them and talk about their childhood stories while they take their meds.
I set strict alarms on their phone and remind them loudly when it's time.

questions.scenario: You are organizing a birthday party for a 5-year-old cousin.

options.text: I am running around serving cake, cleaning spills, and managing the physical chaos.
I keep track of the time, the budget, and make sure we have exactly enough return gifts.
I do the face painting, wear a funny hat, and play games with the kids.
I control the loud kids and make sure nobody ruins the decorations.

questions.scenario: When someone in your friend group is having a panic attack or crying, what do you do?

options.text: I hold their hands, rub their back, and help them breathe.
I ask them logical questions to figure out exactly what triggered the panic.
I hug them, say sweet things, and take them to get an ice cream to cheer them up.
I clear the crowd around them and firmly tell everyone to give them space.

questions.scenario: Which of these 'messy' situations doesn't gross you out?

options.text: Cleaning up someone's vomit or dealing with heavy bleeding.
Looking at complicated, weird skin rashes or medical infections.
Dealing with a baby's dirty diapers and spit-ups.
Dealing with angry, shouting relatives in a hospital lobby.

questions.scenario: You are watching a documentary about a hospital.

options.text: I love the intense siren of the ambulance and the rush to the Emergency Room.
I watch closely how the nurse operates the complex ECG and ventilator machines.
I love seeing the children's ward painted with cartoons and toys.
I admire the Head Nurse who is confidently giving orders to 20 staff members.

questions.scenario: How do you handle your own school assignments and homework?

options.text: I finish them fast in a rush right before the deadline.
I make a highly detailed checklist and cross things out logically.
I use colorful pens, highlights, and draw nice borders.
I finish mine early and then force my friends to complete theirs too.

questions.scenario: If you had to work a 12-hour shift, what would keep you going?

options.text: The adrenaline rush of moving fast and saving lives physically.
The satisfaction of seeing a patient's medical charts getting better.
The smiles and hugs of the people I am taking care of.
The pride of running the whole floor smoothly without a single mistake.

questions.scenario: What is your core personality trait in your family?

options.text: The Action Hero (Always running to help).
The Observer (Always noticing if someone looks sick).
The Comforter (Always giving hugs and making people smile).
The Boss (Always making sure rules are followed).

ER_ICU_Nurse.title: ER / ICU Trauma Nurse
ER_ICU_Nurse.primary_match_text: You are an absolute lifesaver! You thrive on adrenaline, have incredible physical stamina, and stay calm while rushing to help others.
ER_ICU_Nurse.day_in_the_life: Working in the Emergency Room, performing CPR, giving immediate injections, and saving lives in real-time.
ER_ICU_Nurse.alternative_match_text: Because of your quick reflexes and strong heart, you would also make an excellent Paramedic or Armed Forces Medical Assistant.
ER_ICU_Nurse.roadmap: Take Science (PCB) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Nursing, followed by specialized training in Emergency/Critical Care.

Clinical_Nurse_Specialist.title: Clinical Nurse Specialist
Clinical_Nurse_Specialist.primary_match_text: You are the highly analytical caregiver. You love details, tracking data, and ensuring that medical procedures are done flawlessly.
Clinical_Nurse_Specialist.day_in_the_life: Monitoring complex life-support machines, tracking patient vitals exactly, and assisting doctors in deep medical analysis.
Clinical_Nurse_Specialist.alternative_match_text: Your love for medical data and tracking makes you a perfect fit for Healthcare Informatics or Pathology Lab Tech.
Clinical_Nurse_Specialist.roadmap: Take Science (PCB) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Nursing, followed by an M.Sc in Clinical Nursing.

Pediatric_Nurse.title: Pediatric / Childcare Nurse
Pediatric_Nurse.primary_match_text: You have a heart of gold. You are creative, highly empathetic, and know exactly how to make sick people (especially children) smile.
Pediatric_Nurse.day_in_the_life: Working in the children's ward, giving medicines using playful tricks, and comforting scared kids and parents.
Pediatric_Nurse.alternative_match_text: If you want to use your empathy in other fields, you would excel as a Child Psychologist or a Special Education Teacher.
Pediatric_Nurse.roadmap: Take Science (PCB) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Nursing, followed by a diploma/master's in Pediatric Nursing.

Head_Nurse_Matron.title: Head Nurse / Matron (Nursing Administrator)
Head_Nurse_Matron.primary_match_text: You are a born leader with a caring core. You love discipline, organizing things perfectly, and commanding respect from your team.
Head_Nurse_Matron.day_in_the_life: Managing a team of 50 nurses, making duty rosters, ensuring hospital hygiene, and running the ward like a boss.
Head_Nurse_Matron.alternative_match_text: With your commanding nature and organizing skills, you can easily transition into Hospital Administration or Healthcare HR.
Head_Nurse_Matron.roadmap: Take Science (PCB) in 11th/12th. Pursue a B.Sc in Nursing, gain experience, and do an MBA in Hospital Administration.
